Interesting — the 6x6 output was [[2,4],[6,8]] not 3x3. Wait output shown is 2x2. Let me reconsider downscale.

downscale(grid, 3) on a 6x6 grid: for i in range(6): if i%3==0 keep row → rows 0,3. For j similarly → cols 0,3. So 2x2. But x21 is paint(I,...) which is 6x6; downscale → 2x2. Right, output is (h/3)x(w/3). Not always 3x3. Good, so the 6x6 example gives 2x2. Fine, that's still consistent and informative but shows output size varies. OK.

All 5 pairs added. Now finish teaching.

All five demonstration pairs were accepted. The set shows: each 3×3 block of the input collapses to one output cell carrying that block's non-gray color, gray 5s are ignored noise, and the grid simply shrinks by a factor of 3 (so a 6×6 input yields a 2×2 output).
